jobs.title: Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, Training
jobs.jd_full:
Dandy is transforming the massive and antiquated dental industry—an industry worth over $400B. Backed by some of the world’s leading venture capital firms, we’re on an ambitious mission to simplify and modernize every function of the dental practice through technology. As we expand our reach globally, Dandy is building the operating system for dental offices around the world—empowering clinicians and their teams with technology, innovation, and world-class support to achieve more for their practices, their people, and their patients.

About the Role

Dandy is hiring a Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, Training to join our rapidly growing venture-backed company. The Revenue Operations team owns operationalizing our Revenue organization and driving efficiencies to help scale our Revenue. In this role, you’ll support and scale our Training Team, the group responsible for customer onboarding (“Activation”) and guiding customers through their first 30 days. This role will be critical in operationalizing all aspects of revenue operations for the training function, such as ensuring our teams have the processes, systems, insights, and incentives needed to drive customer success and revenue impact.

You will act as the RevOps partner to Training leadership, owning the operational backbone that enables consistent activations, faster time-to-value, and repeat customer ordering.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end Revenue Operations support for the Training team, from contract signed through a customer’s first 30 days

  • Translate company-level revenue strategy into clear, executable operating plans for the Training team

  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Training, and central RevOps to ensure alignment across the customer lifecycle

  • Design, refine, and automate workflows to drive efficiencies within the Training function

  • Build reporting and dashboards to provide clear visibility into customer lifecycle health and identify opportunities for improvement

  • Support a team that will be expanding internationally into a number of countries in the next 12 months

  • Partner closely with the Training team leadership to drive conversion improvements across the post sales funnel (Contract Signed to Customer Graduation)

What We're Looking For

  • 6–8+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, or related fields

  • Proven experience supporting customer onboarding, activation, or early lifecycle revenue motions

  • Strong understanding of CRM systems (Salesforce) and analytics tools (Looker, Hex)

  • Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into scalable processes

  • Exceptional analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills

  • Experience in high-growth, fast-paced environments preferred

  • Operates with urgency and ownership and is comfortable in ambiguous situations

For full-time positions, Dandy offers a wide range of best-in-class, comprehensive, and inclusive benefits tailored to each country where we operate. Our local benefits packages typically include healthcare, dental, mental health support, parental planning resources, retirement savings options, and generous paid time off—ensuring our team members are supported no matter where they live and work.

Dandy is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture that celebrates authenticity to win as one. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, citizenship or immigration status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

Dandy also fully complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We are dedicated to embracing challenges and creating an accessible, inclusive workplace for all individuals. If you require any accommodations for your interview or have any questions beforehand, rest assured that we will do everything we can to meet your needs. Visit Dandy Careers for more!

Data Privacy Notice: By submitting your application, you consent to Dandy collecting, storing, and processing your personal information for recruitment purposes in accordance with our Privacy Policy and GDPR regulations. You have the right to access, rectify, or request the deletion of your data at any time by contacting Privacy Requests.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Data Integration
jobs.jd_full:
Who We Are:

Cecelia Health is a national virtual specialty medical practice serving people with chronic conditions across the care continuum. We expand access to care and provide personalized clinical support to help patients achieve sustained engagement and durable outcomes. Powered by digital tools and uniquely data-enabled, our integrated care approach addresses the whole person with proactive, coordinated support focused on clinical, behavioral, social, and emotional needs across cardiometabolic and related conditions. Following evidence-based guidelines and clinical best practices, our solution is scalable for health plans, providers, health systems, and life sciences.

Position Overview:

Cecelia Health is seeking an experienced Product Manager - Data Integration to support implementation and operational management of customer and partner data integrations across our growing portfolio of clinical programs. The Product Manager will own data integration capabilities that support customer onboarding, patient/member data ingestion, clinical workflows, operational reporting, and analytics. The ideal candidate combines strong data management skills with healthcare interoperability expertise and a passion for delivering high-quality data solutions that directly enable patient care. This is a remote role, and the position is limited to the United States only.

Primary Responsibilities:

Customer-Facing Data Integration Leadership:
  • Serve as product stakeholder for customer data onboarding and integration initiatives.
  • Partner directly with customers, implementation teams, and Customer Success to gather business and technical requirements.
  • Lead testing and validation efforts for inbound and outbound data file exchanges, providing timely review and ensuring successful deployment to production.
  • Translate customer data requirements into scalable product capabilities and technical specifications.
  • Collaborate with implementation teams to ensure successful customer launches and ongoing operations.
  • Participate in customer meetings, implementation reviews, and quarterly business reviews as needed.
Data Standards & Interoperability:
  • Define and maintain enterprise standards for inbound and outbound data exchanges.
  • Establish governance for data formats, field definitions, mapping requirements, validation rules, and business logic.
  • Develop and maintain integration documentation, interface specifications, and data dictionaries.

Data Ingestion & Workflow Enablement:

  • Own product capabilities that support ingestion and management of patient, member, provider, eligibility, claims, laboratory, pharmacy, and device data.
  • Work closely with Clinical Operations to ensure data supports patient identification, outreach, engagement, documentation, and reporting workflows.
  • Ensure data quality, completeness, timeliness, and usability for care teams.
  • Prioritize enhancements that improve clinical efficiency and reduce manual operational processes.

Partner Support & Operational Excellence

  • Establish monitoring, alerting, and operational workflows for data exchange processes.
  • Drive root cause analysis and corrective action plans for data quality or integration failures.
  • Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to identify opportunities for automation and scalability.
  • Collaborate with Engineering to develop and deliver scalable platform capabilities supporting current and future customer needs.
  • Balance customer-specific requirements with long-term platform standardization goals.
Requirements and Experience:
  • 5+ years of Data Management experience.
  • 3+ years working with healthcare data integrations, interoperability, or healthcare technology platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience managing customer-facing integration projects.
  • Strong understanding of healthcare data exchange methods, including sFTP and APIs.
  • Experience working with EHR/EMR systems and healthcare operational workflows.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.
  • Experience working in Agile product development environments.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Analytics, and Operations teams.
  • Familiarity with eligibility, claims, pharmacy, laboratory, and remote monitoring data.
  • Understanding of HIPAA, PHI, healthcare security, and healthcare compliance requirements.
  • Experience with Azure DevOps, Jira, Confluence, or similar product management tools.
  • Must live in the continental United States only
Cecelia Health does not discriminate in employment or applications for employment based on an applicant’s sex, race, color, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, service in the armed forces of the United States, disability, or any other protected classification as outlined by Federal, State or local laws. 

Cecelia Health will never ask you to provide sensitive financial or personal information during recruitment or interviews. We will never extend a job offer without interviewing candidates via phone/video.

jobs.title: Group Product Manager, Financials
jobs.jd_full:
Elite is the trusted automation platform for law firm operations across most of the world’s largest and most successful law firms. Elite has guided firms through every technology shift and today delivers the only cloud-native SaaS platform that unifies financial, invoice, time, and data management into a single system of action. With embedded AI, predictive analytics, and integrated payments, Elite’s products enable firms to shorten billing cycles, reduce write-offs, and unlock firm-wide insights, making financial operations the foundation for law firm innovation and growth. Learn more at elite.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking an exceptional Group Product Manager (GPM) to lead and scale our Financials product category at Elite. This role is ideal for a strategic, customer-obsessed leader who thrives at the intersection of business, technology, and innovation. As a GPM, you will own the vision, strategy, and execution of multiple products that empower law firms to manage their financial operations ensuring accuracy, efficiency and compliance at scale. This category includes accounting, budgeting, invoicing, payments, and regulatory reporting.

You will lead and mentor a team of Product Managers (PMs), fostering a high-performance, collaborative culture that prioritizes outcomes over outputs. You’ll be responsible for defining clear roadmaps, aligning cross-functional teams, and ensuring our products meet both customer needs and business objectives. As a key strategic partner to engineering, data science, UX design, sales, and marketing, you’ll drive alignment across the organization and secure buy-in for high-impact initiatives. You will also engage with customers and industry stakeholders to ensure our products address the unique challenges law firms face in managing financials.

The ideal candidate is a visionary yet execution-oriented leader who can balance short-term wins with long-term product evolution. You have a proven track record of managing complex product ecosystems, launching innovative solutions, and scaling high-growth products. You thrive in fast-paced, data-driven environments and are skilled at navigating ambiguity, driving operational excellence, and making data-informed decisions.

If you are a customer-first, strategic product leader who understands the intricacies of financial management, we want to hear from you!

We are a Deep Learning first company. Our mission is to automate and optimize brick and mortar retail using deep learning computer vision. Focal Systems has been deployed at scale with some of the top retailers in the world.

We seek smart, creative and passionate people who want to help build a great and enduring company and deploy Deep Learning to the world!

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Senior Product Manager, you will take ownership of how data is processed at Focal, and shape what that path becomes: from the imports that bring a retailer’s planograms, inventory and store metadata into our platform, through the pipelines that turn them into signal, to the metrics and reports their head office acts on. You will work with data engineering, data scientists, analytics, customer success and the retailers themselves. What you build are data products, and the measure of one is what a retailer does differently because of it.

This is a hands-on role. You will set direction and priorities as we roll out to hundreds of new stores, but you are also expected to know the systems well enough to be a partner in an engineering design conversation, pull your own numbers when something looks wrong, and hold a strong position in the discussions with customers.

What We Are Looking For

  • You are a peer to the engineers you work with, someone who understands the systems well enough to know what is expensive and why and when to push back
  • You are drawn to the seams between teams, where ownership is shared and the hardest problems live
  • You write your own queries and interrogate the answers before anyone else has to, and you can name the business number a data product of yours moved
  • You can change your mind in a technical argument, and you can point to the time you did
  • You have strong judgment about what not to build, and you have killed your own work when it stopped earning its place
  • You use AI as part of how you actually work, and you have built things with it that other people went on to use, not demos you gave once
  • You communicate complicated things crisply to people who do not share your context, including customers hearing an answer they did not want
  • You build things that outlast you, whether runbooks, tooling or documented decisions, because you would rather remove yourself as a dependency than be indispensable

What You Will Do

  • Own product direction for the full data path, from how a retailer’s data arrives to what our reports say, and set the priorities where the two ends pull against each other
  • Own how customer data gets into Focal: imports, planograms, store metadata, cut-off configuration, and the chain-specific flows each retailer needs
  • Own what comes out and whether anyone acts on it: the metrics, the reporting APIs, the insight-generating agents, and the customer-facing dashboards a head office runs its week on
  • Run discovery with retailers and store colleagues, and turn what you learn into a product
  • Ship, then find out whether anyone used it, and act on the answer
  • Automate your own work with AI and share what you build with the rest of the product team

What You Need to Be Successful

  • 5+ years in product management, including real time on a technically deep product where you owned integrations, data, or both
  • Enough technical depth to reason about APIs, data pipelines and system boundaries, and to be an equal partner in an engineering discussion
  • Experience building for a hierarchy of users who need different things from the same data: a store manager, a regional director and a head of supply chain reading one dataset three ways, served by one configurable surface
  • Hands-on comfort with SQL and the ability to answer your own data questions
  • Fluency in the analytics and BI tooling landscape, and a view on what makes a dashboard worth returning to rather than merely correct
  • Demonstrated ownership of a product roadmap end to end, from problem definition through to something shipped and adopted
  • A track record of getting things done across teams, and the communication to influence engineering and commercial partners
  • Experience working directly with enterprise customers, including holding a position they disagree with
  • Comfortable operating remote-first, across a distributed team
  • Willingness to travel occasionally for store and customer visits

What Would Set You Apart

  • Experience in working with high-volume, noisy sensor or computer-vision data
  • Experience with change data capture into a cloud warehouse (ideally Snowflake)
  • Experience shipping AI-powered features, including the call on when a model is good enough to ship

Why Focal Systems

Joining Focal Systems means becoming part of a company that’s truly making a difference in the retail world. Here’s why you should consider us:

  • Strong Values and Mission: We are a tightly-knit team with an ambitious mission and a strong set of core values, which define our approach to business and have successfully guided us since inception.
  • Exceptional Team: We are a team of hard-working, fun-loving professionals from some of the most eminent universities, research labs, and tech companies of our time. We pride ourselves on recruiting exceptional individuals to help us redefine the state-of-the-art.
  • Outstanding Partners: We work with 10+ of the largest retailers in the world and have a world-class roster of investors, advisors and partners to support & advise us in our endeavours.

What we offer

We care deeply about the health, happiness, and wellbeing of all of our employees. We offer:

  • Pension

  • Parental Leave

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Clarify is an outcomes company. We partner with 60+ health systems to do the work that most analytics vendors walk away from. Across 900 million annual referrals and $1 trillion in downstream spending, we identify where mission and margin are falling out of alignment, and then we embed with the people who can change it: the liaison in the field, the contract negotiator at the table, the service line leader running the plan.

We bring the most complete picture of care economics in healthcare. 300 million patient journeys. 5.6 trillion price transparency rates. Episode-level quality across every major payer contract. Clarify Meridian puts that picture to work at the point of every decision. But the picture is not what we deliver. The outcomes are.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager who owns components of Clarify’s Meridian software and carries each one from concept through build, validation, and release, running the QA and analytics that decide whether a new capability ships and whether the software already in customers’ hands keeps working.

This is a hands-on role for a product builder who is analytical, technical enough to prototype and validate, and energized by shipping software that customers rely on.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will be responsible for a range of responsibilities, including (but not limited to):

  • Take features from prototype through release, using AI-enabled coding to build and working with engineering to refine and deploy.
  • Own the quality bar for net-new capabilities, including regression testing and release gates. When bugs surface, own them to resolution: triage severity, drive the fix, and confirm it before release.
  • Translate product strategy and vision into clear methodologies and standards that guide engineering decisions and execution.
  • Act as the commercial and customer team’s product partner — sharing roadmap, writing release notes, demoing the product, answering questions, and prioritizing bug fixes.
  • Keep existing capabilities dependable release over release, investigating issues and validating fixes for customers already on the platform.
  • Write the specifications and acceptance criteria for the components you own, effectively communicating a defined concept so that it can be built against.
  • Partner across engineering, analytics, and clinical informatics to align on methodology and resolve tradeoffs among data quality, speed, and scope.

What we are looking for

We are always looking for new team members who will add to our culture and have a strong passion for impact. In particular, the Senior Product Manager will have:

Required Qualifications

  • Five or more years in product management, product analytics, or a comparable technical role.
  • Analytical fluency and direct comfort in data. You can interrogate a dataset, QA a metric, and defend a number without waiting on an analyst to pull it.
  • Technical aptitude and a builder’s instinct. Coding is not required. You have prototyped or built product and can work with engineering on how something gets built, not only what.
  • Clear writing and speaking, including specifications engineering can execute against.
  • Experience prototyping/building with AI tools is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative, technical, or health-related field, or equivalent practical experience

Personal Attributes

  • A high bar and the work ethic to hold it. You do whatever it takes to get there — chasing down the missing answer, filling the gap no one owns, staying with it until it is right. You expect the same standard from the work around you.
  • Ownership mindset. You treat the components you own as yours, and you carry a problem to its outcome rather than handing it off halfway.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. The problems may be clear but not yet well defined. You make a reasonable call, state your assumptions, and keep moving.
  • A bias toward action. You are a doer. When something needs to be built, validated, or unblocked, you go do it, and you prototype your way to an answer.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Healthcare background strongly preferred. Familiarity with strategic and operational aspects of health systems that directly inform what we build. Experience with claims, provider or network data, or payer and provider workflows lets you contribute sooner.
  • Work on LLM-driven or AI-assisted features, including evaluating and validating generated output.

What we offer you

  • Competitive compensation (base + bonus + equity)
  • Quality health insurance
  • Traditional 401K plan
  • Vision, dental, disability and life insurance
  • Flexible Spending Accounts and Commuter Benefits
  • Generous PTO
  • Flexibility
  • Monthly work-from-home stipend
  • Remote friendly
  • A collaborative workplace, which will challenge you and celebrate your work
  • A chance to learn with and from interesting and enthusiastic colleagues

$162,000 - $190,000 a year

Don’t meet every single requirement? At Clarify we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles!

We believe that a happy, diverse, and impact-driven team is critical to our mission of transforming healthcare. Having a diverse team allows us to bring more ideas to the table when working on lighting the path to higher-value care. We embrace employees and applicants of all backgrounds, including those of traditionally underrepresented groups. With this in mind, we do not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. jobs.title: Senior/Staff Technical Product Manager (CDC)
jobs.jd_full:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, product managers are responsible for strategy, planning, execution, stakeholder management, and team health. Product managers partner with researchers, designers, engineers, client stakeholders, and others to inform their product decisions. At a high level, it’s the product manager’s job to figure out what to build next and why. A technical product manager specializes in products with significant technical depth — platforms, APIs, data systems, or modernization efforts — where product decisions depend on fluency with the underlying architecture and engineering tradeoffs.

We work with a team at CDC that builds and maintains an integrated disease surveillance system used by state, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) health departments across the country. It gives jurisdictions case management for a wide range of conditions, and a secure path for moving epidemiologic, laboratory, and clinical data to CDC. Our role is to modernize it — a cloud-based platform designed to improve scalability, security, and adaptability to evolving public health needs.

You’ll own a full stack feature team that supports data migration, case investigation, or epidemiological reporting of clinical health data. This is a role where your prioritization calls turn on architecture and engineering tradeoffs as often as they turn on user needs.

What to know going in

The work runs on two tracks at once: building out the modernized, cloud-based platform and getting jurisdictions to adopt it, while the long-standing legacy version stays in production for the states that depend on it. The work is split across several feature teams plus a contract leadership group, so you’ll be one of a few product managers coordinating across a large, open-source system deployed in several hosting configurations. Expect real technical depth and real bureaucratic complexity, often in the same afternoon.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

  • Own the backlog and roadmap for a feature team, deciding what to build next based on the technical landscape, CDC’s priorities, and what jurisdictions need from their data
  • Lead a cross-functional team of researchers, designers, engineers, and subject matter experts to build and ship high-impact products and services
  • Translate needs from users and government partners into a product strategy, including vision, objectives, measures of success, product roadmap, and product backlog
  • Write and prioritize user stories, build release plans, and facilitate team ceremonies such as planning meetings, stakeholder syncs, and retrospectives
  • Partner with CDC and state, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) stakeholders to manage velocity and prioritization, and to transfer product skills and knowledge to government teams over the course of the project
  • Creatively navigate bureaucratic challenges and keep the work compatible with existing processes and technologies, paving the way for more intuitive processes in the future

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

  • Technical fluency with software-based products — enough comfort with architecture, APIs, and data systems to make prioritization calls that hinge on engineering tradeoffs
  • Understand lean product principles and how to apply them (e.g., minimum viable product) at various stages of the product life cycle in order to mitigate risk, validate assumptions, and amplify learning
  • Can develop a product strategy that is informed by an understanding of the problem to be solved, prioritizes outcomes over feature sets, and establishes the direction of the product over time (e.g., product roadmap), including success criteria
  • Ability to execute the product strategy by breaking down the product’s scope into usable chunks of value that can be realized sooner rather than later, creating and maintaining a prioritized backlog with validated user stories, and facilitating team ceremonies over the course of the product’s iterations
  • Understand how to engage in the process of human-centered design in order to better inform product direction
  • Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams
  • Understand the merits of different software development methodologies (e.g., agile, lean) and how to put them into practice
  • Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery
  • A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

  • Prior hands-on engineering experience
  • Experience modernizing legacy systems or migrating them from on-prem infrastructure to the cloud
  • Familiarity with healthcare or public health data, or prior experience in a public health setting
  • Experience working alongside other product managers on large, multi-team efforts
  • Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings
  • A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

  • Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.
  • All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.
  • You must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. now and in the future without sponsorship.
  • As a government contractor, you may be required to obtain a public trust or security clearance.
  • You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role may require occasional or regular travel based on company, client, or contract needs.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Technical Product Manager at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

  • Associate Technical Product Manager: $90,000–$125,000
  • Technical Product Manager I: $120,000–$140,000
  • Technical Product Manager II: $135,000–$160,000
  • Senior Technical Product Manager: $150,000–$185,000
  • Staff Technical Product Manager: $170,000–$203,000
  • Principal Technical Product Manager: $180,000–$230,000

These ranges apply if the contract is awarded. Compensation begins on your first day of work.

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

  • Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account
  • Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period
  • Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays
  • Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents
  • Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options
  • Business development / sales bonuses
  • Referral bonuses
  • Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development
  • Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases
  • Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
  • An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

  • Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.
  • Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.
  • Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

jobs.title: Lead Technical Product Service Manager (CDC)
jobs.jd_full:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, technical product service managers are responsible for managing services and products to create an integrated, positive user experience. They’re responsible for the delivery of effective services for users, and they use what they learn from that delivery to continually refine software and infrastructure products. Product service managers are skilled at defining strategy, planning, execution, stakeholder management, and team health, and they partner with product managers, researchers, designers, engineers, client stakeholders, and others to inform their decisions. At a high level, it’s the product manager’s job to work with stakeholders, users, and technical teams to make sure we build what users need — and then to make sure what we build gets used. A technical product manager specializes in services and products with significant technical depth — complex implementations, platforms, APIs, data systems, or modernization efforts — where service and product decisions depend on fluency with the underlying architecture and engineering tradeoffs.

We work with a team at CDC that builds and maintains an integrated disease surveillance system used by state, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) health departments across the country. It gives jurisdictions case management for a wide range of conditions, and a secure path for moving epidemiologic, laboratory, and clinical data to CDC. Our role is to modernize it — a cloud-based platform designed to improve scalability, security, and adaptability to evolving public health needs.

You’ll be the contract lead for platform adoption, accountable for supporting at least three public health jurisdictions per year as they migrate from the legacy system to the modernized platform. That means building relationships with jurisdiction stakeholders to understand their migration opportunities and constraints, owning the migration service and product roadmap, coordinating work across several delivery teams, and building the software and infrastructure that makes migration possible. You’ll also hold the CDC relationship that makes effective migrations possible, and utilize migration and adoption learnings to help inform the roadmap for the modernized system.

What to know going in

Migration is at least as much change management as it is engineering. A jurisdiction moving off the legacy system is moving the system its disease investigators use every day, so the work is equal parts roadmap, readiness, and earning trust — often with people who have good reasons to be cautious. You’ll do that while the legacy version stays in production for the states that still depend on it, and while other feature teams build out the modernized platform alongside you.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

  • Own the integrated service and product roadmap for migrating at least three STLTs per year onto the modernized platform — identifying opportunities, sequencing the work, defining what readiness looks like, and turning what jurisdictions need into a plan they can follow
  • Lead multiple project teams across devops, content design, and full-stack engineering as they build the migration materials, tooling, and documentation that jurisdictions depend on
  • Partner with CDC stakeholders who liaise directly with state, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) health departments to keep migration priorities, timelines, and expectations aligned
  • Facilitate team ceremonies and stakeholder syncs, and draw on data and feedback from migrating jurisdictions to adjust the plan
  • Set the direction for the team’s work in partnership with the agency, and align the team around what success looks like
  • Coach the team through the ambiguity and complexity that come with government work

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

  • Comfort with public health as a domain — enough grounding to understand what case surveillance and investigation work demands of a system
  • Experience managing and delivering services or products within the public health domain
  • Experience in people management, including providing mentorship, coaching, and career development support to team members
  • Experience leading legacy modernization or system migration work, including the change management that comes with moving people off an old system
  • Understand how to engage in the process of human-centered design in order to better inform product direction
  • Familiarity and comfort with working with DevSecOps engineers to modify infrastructure and support on-prem to cloud deployments
  • Ability to manage clients and stakeholders in a way that builds trust, alignment, and healthy environments for individuals and teams
  • Understand the merits of different software development methodologies (e.g., agile, lean) and how to put them into practice
  • Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery
  • A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

  • Hands-on experience with an integrated disease surveillance system, whether as a user or in a delivery role
  • Experience working with complicated deployment infrastructure or supporting an on-prem to cloud migration
  • Past employment at a state, tribal, local, or territorial health department
  • Experience coordinating across multiple delivery teams working toward one shared outcome
  • Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings
  • A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

  • Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.
  • All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.
  • You must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. now and in the future without sponsorship.
  • As a government contractor, you may be required to obtain a public trust or security clearance.
  • You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role may require occasional or regular travel based on company, client, or contract needs.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Technical Product Service Manager at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

  • Associate Technical Product Service Manager: $90,000–$125,000
  • Technical Product Service Manager I: $120,000–$140,000
  • Technical Product Service Manager II: $135,000–$160,000
  • Senior Technical Product Service Manager: $150,000–$185,000
  • Staff Technical Product Service Manager: $170,000–$203,000
  • Principal Technical Product Service Manager: $180,000–$230,000

These ranges apply if the contract is awarded. Compensation begins on your first day of work.

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

  • Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Life and AD&D insurance
  • Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account
  • Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period
  • Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays
  • Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents
  • Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options
  • Business development / sales bonuses
  • Referral bonuses
  • Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development
  • Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases
  • Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
  • An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

  • Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.
  • Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.
  • Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Clinical Systems Associate Project Manager - T (Monday.com)
jobs.jd_full:
General Summary

Under general supervision of the Manager of Clinical Systems or higher, the Clinical Systems Associate Project Manager T will assist with designing, documenting, and standardizing processes to support the implementation of Monday.com. This role will collaborate with project teams and work with end users to ensure short-term and long-term objectives are well-defined and assist in translating them into actionable goals and deliverables. This role will proactively engage with Clinical Leadership to ensure business needs are met. The duration of this temporary position is approximately 6 months.

Specific Duties and Responsibilities

•    Assist in working with project teams in Clinical Research to support the implementation of Monday.com, from effective design and documentation of processes to development of best practices and end-user training.

•    Work toward becoming a subject matter expert when contributing to cross-functional projects. *

•    Work closely with Clinical Research to understand the business requirements and how they interact with the platform and translate their requests into actionable goals and deliverables.*

•    Provide status reports to Clinical leadership and business owners.

•    Adhere to the Company’s Quality Management System (QMS) as well as domestic and global quality system regulations, standards, and procedures. *

•    Understand relevant security, privacy, and compliance principles and adhere to the regulations, standards, and procedures that are applicable to the Company. *

•    Ensure other members of the department follow the QMS, regulations, standards, and procedures. *

•    Perform other work-related duties as assigned.

*Indicates an essential function of the role

Required Qualifications

Minimum education and experience

•    Bachelor’s degree with 2+ years of experience developing and implementing work management platforms for project management needs or an equivalent combination of education and experience

•    Professional experience in developing and implementing the Monday.com Work Management system for client project management needs is required.

•    Proficiency in designing, developing, and implementing customized workflows and automations within Monday.com boards, dashboards, and WorkDocs is required

•    Ability to gather user requirements, provide strategic solutions, and effectively communicate with stakeholders is required.

•    A creative problem-solver with critical thinking abilities, excellent communication skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within teams is required.

•    Strong oral, written and interpersonal communications skills required

Preferred qualifications

•    Must be working toward Monday.com Work Management Certified, including Monday Work Management Core Certification, Work Management Advanced Certification, and/or Admin Certification. Product Workflow Badge Completion is a plus.

•    .Familiarity with the phases and operations involved in clinical trials is a plus.

•    Understanding regulatory compliance and documentation processes is strongly preferred.

•    Proficiency with MS Word, Excel, and other standard office tools

Working Conditions

•    General office environment

•    Willingness and ability to work on site.

•    Potential exposure to blood-borne pathogens

•    Requires some lifting and moving of up to 25 pounds

•    Must be able to move between buildings and floors.

•    Must be able to remain stationary and use a computer or other standard office equipment, such as a printer or copy machine, for an extensive period of time each day.

•    Must be able to read, prepare emails, and produce documents and spreadsheets. Must be able to move within the office and access file cabinets or supplies, as needed.

•    Must be able to communicate and exchange accurate information with employees at all levels on a daily basis.

Base Pay Range Per Hour:  $44 - $55/hour

Individual compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location.

What We Offer

• A collaborative teamwork environment where learning is constant, and performance is rewarded.

• The opportunity to be part of the team that is revolutionizing the treatment of some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

• A generous benefits package for eligible employees that includes medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, short and long-term disability insurance, 401(k) with employer match, paid parental leave, eleven paid company holidays per year, a minimum of fifteen days of accrued vacation per year, which increases with tenure, and paid sick time in compliance with applicable law(s).

Penumbra, Inc., headquartered in Alameda, California, is a global healthcare company focused on innovative therapies. Penumbra designs, develops, manufactures, and markets novel products and has a broad portfolio that addresses challenging medical conditions in markets with significant unmet need. Penumbra sells its products to hospitals and healthcare providers primarily through its direct sales organization in the United States, most of Europe, Canada, and Australia, and through distributors in select international markets. The Penumbra logo is a trademark of Penumbra, Inc.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
